header: Meeting: POC scoping - open models and shortlist | Date/Time: 2026-12-10 14:00 PST | Duration: 45 minutes | Redwood: Sophie Chen (AE), Daniel Park (SE) | Mira Analytics: Laura, Raj, Emilia, Omar
summary: AE+SE from Redwood ran a POC scoping call with Mira Analytics to align on success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks and timelines for a 4-week POC using open models. Key constraints: multi-lingual support (EN/ES/FR + occasional JP), domain-specific medical/analytics terminology, EU data residency preference and SOC2/ISO requirements. Shortlist of open models proposed (Llama 3 small/medium trimmed, Mistral Instruct, Mosaic MPT-7B-Instruct, Falcon-40B variants) with tradeoffs in latency, cost and accuracy. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send security pack and benchmark harness, Mira to send labeled prompts, kickoff POC week of 2026-12-15.
topics: Benchmark plan (p95 latency, throughput, hallucination/accuracy on domain eval)
Model shortlist and quality tradeoffs (open models)
Infrastructure choices: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC
transcript:
[00:00] Sophie Chen (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for jumping on. quick intro - i'm sophie, i'm the AE supporting mira's POC. Daniel (SE) is with me for the technical scoping.
[00:06] Laura Kim (Mira): hi - Laura here. we wanted to get aligned on how a 4-week POC would look, and what open models you recommend for our analytics assistant.
[00:12] Daniel Park (Redwood): great. goal for today: agree success criteria, workload sizing, shortlist models, and define the benchmark plan and timeline.
[00:20] Raj Patel (Mira): for context our workload is customer-facing analytics queries, short prompts (~10-80 tokens) plus some longer generation for summaries (~300 tokens). expect peak ~25 qps, average 6 qps. monthly tokens roughly 200M tokens.
[00:34] Emilia Torres (Mira): also multilingual - ~15% spanish, 5% french, occasional japanese. domain vocabulary includes medical device and regulatory terms.
[00:43] Omar Singh (Mira): security note - we need EU data residency for logs and test datasets; SOC2 is required and we may need an on-prem option if redacted data leaves the region.
[00:55] Daniel Park (Redwood): understood. we can run the POC against Redwood Hosted for fastest path, or Dedicated / Private if you need VPC/EU only. for benchmarks we plan p95 latency, throughput (tokens/sec), and quality metrics vs your gold labels - plus hallucination checks.
[01:10] Laura: success criteria we care about: p95 latency for short queries under 250-300ms, overall accuracy/utility on labeled set above 85% (per your scoring), and cost target — ideally <$50 per 1M tokens for inference.
[01:25] Sophie: that helps. i'll flag cost is variable depending on model size and quantization. part of the POC is to test 2-3 model variants to trade off latency vs quality.
[01:35] Raj: what models do you suggest for open model shortlist? we've looked at Llama variants and Mistral in our own research.
[01:40] Daniel: our initial shortlist for the POC: Llama 3-family trimmed to small/medium for latency; Mistral Instruct (7B) for strong cost/quality; Mosaic MPT-7B-Instruct for instruction-friendly outputs; and Falcon-40B-instruct as a higher-quality baseline if you want to test a bigger open model. we can also include a quantized 8-bit Llama 2/3 to compare.
[01:59] Emilia: how do you evaluate hallucination and domain accuracy for those models?
[02:03] Daniel: we'll run your 500 labeled prompts through each model and compute precision/recall style metrics on structured outputs plus a hallucination rate metric — e.g., percent of generated facts not present in gold labels. we'll also run scenario-based tests for multi-turn context and prefix caching to simulate long sessions.
[02:21] Laura: speaking of caching, our traffic pattern is bursty with interactive sessions; latency on cold starts matters. do you support KV cache across sessions?
[02:29] Daniel: yes, Redwood runtime supports KV cache management and prefix caching; for Dedicated / Private we can tune cache eviction policies. that reduces per-token compute for multi-turn flows. in hosted POC we'll instrument cache hit rates.
[02:43] Omar: on encryption/KMS — do you support customer-managed keys for logs and models?
[02:47] Sophie: yes, for Private we support KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. we'll include the security pack with specifics.
[02:53] Raj: what's the realistic throughput and latency for e.g., Mistral 7B vs Falcon 40B on your hosted infra?
[02:59] Daniel: rough ballpark — Mistral 7B quantized on our optimized runtime often hits p95 ~120-200ms for short prompts at 1-2 token generation latency plus network; throughput depends on batch config but can do 20-30 qps for small prompts. Falcon-40B even quantized might be ~300-500ms p95 and lower qps unless on larger dedicated GPUs; cost will be materially higher.
[03:20] Laura: we need to validate multilingual quality—some of our Spanish prompts include domain-specific terms. any preference in models?
[03:26] Daniel: Mistral and Llama-family tend to have decent multilingual coverage, but performance varies. part of the POC we'll include language buckets and per-lang scoring. if Japanese is critical, Falcon variants sometimes do better but with cost tradeoffs.
[03:39] Emilia: timeline — you said 4 weeks? can you break down activities?
[03:42] Sophie: yes: Week 0 (kickoff + access) quick infra setup; Week 1 run baseline benchmarks across shortlisted models + smoke tests; Week 2 run domain evals with your labeled set and iterate prompt tuning; Week 3 integration tests (latency under load, caching, failover), Week 4 wrap-up, cost analysis, and final recommendation. target report by end of week 4.
[04:04] Raj: do we need dedicated capacity for the POC? we're not sure yet.
[04:08] Daniel: not strictly. we recommend starting hosted for speed; if benchmarks show you need lower jitter or dedicated GPUs to hit p95 targets, we can spin up Dedicated for a limited POC window. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation but requires a slightly longer setup.
[04:23] Laura: what about eval harness — how will you run the tests, do we need to provide infra?
[04:27] Daniel: we will provide a benchmark harness (python scripts + docker) that hits the Redwood API with configurable concurrency, prompt sets, and records latency/throughput and token counts. you'll run locally or we can run from our infra against your test dataset if you prefer. we'll also provide result artifacts and a scoring spreadsheet.
[04:45] Sophie: i'll include pricing bands: hosted per-token pricing per model variant, and a Dedicated POC cost estimate. note that quantized models and batching can bring costs down significantly.
[04:55] Omar: security follow-up — we need to see SOC2 report and a data flow diagram showing where logs and artifacts live. also need SSO/SAML details for auth and RBAC.
[05:06] Sophie: we'll attach SOC2/ISO certs and a high-level architecture diagram. for SSO we support SAML/SCIM and RBAC roles.
[05:14] Raj: any pitfalls we should be aware of? e.g., tokenization differences with domain terms?
[05:19] Daniel: yes tokenization and subword splitting can affect domain terms; we'll surface rare token handling, and may use light fine-tuning or instruction tuning if necessary. for many POCs prompt engineering + LLM reranking can solve a lot without full fine-tune.
[05:33] Emilia: how do you measure hallucination quantitatively?
[05:36] Daniel: we'll compare generated facts to your gold labels; for open-ended outputs we'll use a checklist and a human sample audit. we also compute an uncertainty score via logprob thresholds to flag low-confidence outputs.
[05:48] Laura: ok, sounds reasonable. what's the expected time to get initial numbers once you have our prompts?
[05:53] Daniel: we can run baseline runs within 48 hours of receiving the labeled set, and get a first-cut report in 72 hours. full integration tests and cost analysis take the remainder of the 4 weeks.
[06:04] Sophie: recapping next steps: we'll send security pack & pricing by 12/12, benchmark harness by 12/13, and plan kickoff week of 12/15.
[06:15] Laura: confirmed. one more question — do you support model quantization to int8 / 4-bit and do you provide guidance on quality delta?
[06:22] Daniel: yes we support 8-bit and some 4-bit paths; we'll show quality vs latency/cost tradeoffs in the POC. typically 8-bit has minimal quality loss for many tasks, 4-bit can increase hallucination risk on some domain facts — we'll quantify that.
[06:38] Omar: about data residency — if we need EU-only telemetry, is that doable for hosted?
[06:42] Sophie: we have EU regions for Hosted and a Private deployment option for strict residency. we'll include the options in the security doc.
[06:50] Emilia: would you recommend any model to skip for our use-case?
[06:53] Daniel: probably skip larger unfine-tuned open models that are expensive without noticeable domain gains. start with Mistral 7B, Llama 3 small/med, MPT-7B Instr, and one higher-capacity Falcon-40B only as a control.
[07:07] Raj: ok that seems like a good plan. thanks.
[07:09] Sophie: great. we'll follow-up with calendar invites for the kickoff and attach docs. thanks everyone.
[07:15] Laura: thanks, bye.
questions: Q: What are Mira's exact latency and cost targets? A: p95 < 250-300ms for short queries, cost < $50 per 1M tokens targeted for inference.\nQ: Multilingual priority? A: EN primary, ES secondary, FR and JP occasional — measure per-lang performance.\nQ: POC timeline? A: 4-week POC with kickoff week of 2026-12-15.
